date: "2026-10-10"

---

Same code as crashdata_clean.Rmd, rearranged. Each chunk notes which crashdata_clean Part it came from.

* **Setup and import (Parts 1-3)**
* **Analysis (Parts 4-25):** every table, with its preview chart
* **Article fact checks 1-6:** in order
* **Flourish graphics 1-6:** in order. Each one has two chunks:
    * **A** exports the raw table
    * **B** builds on A and exports `flourish_N_....csv`, which is the file to upload to Flourish
* **Other exports:** CSVs that aren't Flourish graphics

Run the chunks top to bottom.

# Setup and import

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(rio)
library(lubridate)
library(janitor)
library(openxlsx)
library(tidycensus)

# all exported CSVs go into the "output" folder (created here if it doesn't exist)
dir.create("output", showWarnings = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#PART 1 IMPORT DATA (clean Part 1)
# 2024-2026 ACRS 2.0 data, downloaded one year per file (Oct 6, 2026).
# The 2026 files live in "2026 latest download". When you re-download 2026, rename the old folder
# (e.g. "2026 download Oct 6") and put the new files in a fresh "2026 latest download" folder;
# nothing in this file needs to change. Current 2026 download: Oct. 6, 2026.

# ---- read each year separately (all columns as text so the years stack cleanly) ----
report_2024_only <- read_tsv('2024-2026_dashboard/2024 Crash Map_Reports_data.csv', locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-16LE"), col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
report_2025_only <- read_tsv('2024-2026_dashboard/2025 Crash Map_Reports_data.csv', locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-16LE"), col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
report_2026_only <- read_tsv('2024-2026_dashboard/2026 latest download/2026 Crash Map_Reports_data.csv', locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-16LE"), col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))

contribs_2024_only <- read_tsv('2024-2026_dashboard/2024 Crash Map_Contributing Circumstances_data.csv', locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-16LE"), col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
contribs_2025_only <- read_tsv('2024-2026_dashboard/2025 Crash Map_Contributing Circumstances_data.csv', locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-16LE"), col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
contribs_2026_only <- read_tsv('2024-2026_dashboard/2026 latest download/2026 Crash Map_Contributing Circumstances_data.csv', locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-16LE"), col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))

occupants_2024_only <- read_tsv('2024-2026_dashboard/2024 Crash Map_Occupants_data.csv', locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-16LE"), col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
occupants_2025_only <- read_tsv('2024-2026_dashboard/2025 Crash Map_Occupants_data.csv', locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-16LE"), col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
occupants_2026_only <- read_tsv('2024-2026_dashboard/2026 latest download/2026 Crash Map_Occupants_data.csv', locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-16LE"), col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))

nonmotorists_2024_only <- read_tsv('2024-2026_dashboard/2024 Crash Map_NonMotorists_data.csv', locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-16LE"), col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
nonmotorists_2025_only <- read_tsv('2024-2026_dashboard/2025 Crash Map_NonMotorists_data.csv', locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-16LE"), col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
nonmotorists_2026_only <- read_tsv('2024-2026_dashboard/2026 latest download/2026 Crash Map_NonMotorists_data.csv', locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-16LE"), col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))

vehicles_2024_only <- read_tsv('2024-2026_dashboard/2024 Crash Map_Vehicles_data.csv', locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-16LE"), col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
vehicles_2025_only <- read_tsv('2024-2026_dashboard/2025 Crash Map_Vehicles_data.csv', locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-16LE"), col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
vehicles_2026_only <- read_tsv('2024-2026_dashboard/2026 latest download/2026 Crash Map_Vehicles_data.csv', locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-16LE"), col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))

# ---- stack the three years, then let R guess the column types once on the combined table ----
report_2024                     <- bind_rows(report_2024_only, report_2025_only, report_2026_only) |> type_convert()
contributing_circumstances_2024 <- bind_rows(contribs_2024_only, contribs_2025_only, contribs_2026_only) |> type_convert()
occupants_2024                  <- bind_rows(occupants_2024_only, occupants_2025_only, occupants_2026_only) |> type_convert()
nonmotorists_2024               <- bind_rows(nonmotorists_2024_only, nonmotorists_2025_only, nonmotorists_2026_only) |> type_convert()
vehicles_2024                   <- bind_rows(vehicles_2024_only, vehicles_2025_only, vehicles_2026_only) |> type_convert()

#remove rows
rm(list = ls(pattern = "_only$"))
```

```{r}
#PART 2 Import Data (clean Part 2)

# ---- import the older eras ----
# 2015-2018: one Excel file per year, sheet "CRASH", 9 columns
crash_2015 <- import('2015-2018/Crash_2015date and time.xlsx', which = 'CRASH')
crash_2016 <- import('2015-2018/Crash_2016date and time.xlsx', which = 'CRASH')
crash_2017 <- import('2015-2018/Crash_2017date and time.xlsx', which = 'CRASH')
crash_2018 <- import('2015-2018/Crash_2018date and time.xlsx', which = 'CRASH')

# despite the "2019" filename, this one file holds 2019 THROUGH 2023
report_2019 <- read_tsv('2019-2023 dashboard/2019 CrashMap_REPORT_data.csv',
                        locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-16LE"))
```

```{r}
#PART 3 year-to-date cutoff (clean Part 3)
# Change these two numbers to move the year-to-date cutoff everywhere in this file.
# Every YTD comparison runs Jan 1 through this month/day, in every year.
ytd_month <- 9
ytd_day   <- 30

# readable version for chart titles, e.g. "Sep 18"
ytd_label <- paste(month.abb[ytd_month], ytd_day)

# safety check: warn if the cutoff is later than the newest data
last_data_date <- max(mdy(report_2024$Crashdate))
if (make_date(year(last_data_date), ytd_month, ytd_day) > last_data_date)
  warning("YTD cutoff (", ytd_label, ") is after the last day of data (", last_data_date, ")")

ytd_label
```

# Analysis

```{r}
#Part 4 Graph Year to date for all years collected (clean Part 4)

crashes_all_years <- bind_rows(
  # 2015-2018: date is "06-15-2015" text; severity lives in REPORT_TYPE
  bind_rows(crash_2015, crash_2016, crash_2017, crash_2018) |>
    transmute(crash_date = mdy(ACC_DATE),
              is_fatal   = REPORT_TYPE == "Fatal Crash"),

  # 2019-2023: severity is Reporttype, same wording
  report_2019 |>
    transmute(crash_date = mdy(Crashdate),
              is_fatal   = Reporttype == "Fatal Crash"),

  # 2024-2026: ACRS 2.0 renamed it, and pluralized the value
  report_2024 |>
    transmute(crash_date = mdy(Crashdate),
              is_fatal   = `Crash Severity Description` == "Fatal Crashes")
) |>
  mutate(year = year(crash_date)) |>
  filter(!is.na(crash_date))

# ---- year to date, Jan 1 through the YTD cutoff (Part 3) of each year ----
ytd_all_years <- crashes_all_years |>
  filter(crash_date <= make_date(year, ytd_month, ytd_day)) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(total_crashes = n(),
            fatal_crashes = sum(is_fatal, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  mutate(pct_fatal = round(100 * fatal_crashes / total_crashes, 2))

ytd_all_years
```

```{r}
#Part 5 Graph Preview (clean Part 5)
ggplot(ytd_all_years, aes(x = year, y = fatal_crashes)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, color = "#2a78d6") +
  # hollow point for 2026 to mark it as provisional
  geom_point(aes(fill = year == 2026), shape = 21, size = 3,
             color = "#2a78d6", stroke = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#fcfcfb", "FALSE" = "#2a78d6"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2015:2026) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +      # anchor at zero so the rises/falls stay honest
  labs(title = paste0("Maryland fatal crashes, Jan 1 - ", ytd_label),
       subtitle = "2026 is incomplete: fatal cases take months to finalize",
       x = NULL, y = "fatal crashes") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
```

```{r}
#Part 6 Graph full-year fatal crashes, 2015-2025 (no 2026) (clean Part 6)
# >>> full_year becomes FLOURISH GRAPHIC 3 (exported in 3A / 3B)

full_year <- crashes_all_years |>
  filter(year >= 2015, year <= 2025) |>       # drop 2026 -- it's only a partial year
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(total_crashes = n(),
            fatal_crashes = sum(is_fatal, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  mutate(pct_fatal = round(100 * fatal_crashes / total_crashes, 2))

full_year

ggplot(full_year, aes(x = year, y = fatal_crashes)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, color = "#2a78d6") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, color = "#2a78d6") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2015:2025) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(title = "Maryland fatal crashes, full year",
       subtitle = "2015-2025",
       x = NULL, y = "fatal crashes") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
```

```{r}
#Part 7 Graph all fatal crashes with 2026 graph stopping early as data runs out (clean Part 7)
# >>> fatal_crashes_daily is not a Flourish graphic; it is exported in OTHER EXPORTS

# last day the data covers (any crash, not just fatal) -- 2026 line stops here
last_date <- max(mdy(report_2024$Crashdate))

#NonTrafficFatal == N filters out all crashes that did not happen on a road, for instance a parking lot
fatal_crashes_daily <- report_2024 |>
  filter(NonTrafficFatal == "N",
         `Crash Severity Description` == "Fatal Crashes") |>
  mutate(crash_date = mdy(Crashdate),
         year = year(crash_date),
         date = format(crash_date, "%m-%d")) |>
  count(date, year) |>
  # add every calendar day, with 0 on days with no fatal crashes
  # (2024 is used because it's a leap year, so Feb 29 is included)
  complete(date = format(seq(ymd("2024-01-01"), ymd("2024-12-31"), by = "day"), "%m-%d"),
           year,
           fill = list(n = 0)) |>
  arrange(date) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  mutate(total = cumsum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(-n) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = total) |>
  # blank out 2026 after the last day of data
  mutate(`2026` = if_else(date > format(last_date, "%m-%d"), NA, `2026`))

fatal_crashes_daily
```

```{r}
#Part 8 Graph preview (clean Part 8)
fatal_crashes_daily |>
  pivot_longer(-date, names_to = "year", values_to = "total") |>
  # use 2024 as a stand-in year so R can plot month-day on a date axis
  mutate(plot_date = ymd(paste0("2024-", date))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = plot_date, y = total, color = year)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b", date_breaks = "1 month") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("2024" = "#86b6ef",
                                "2025" = "#3987e5",
                                "2026" = "#0d366b"),
                     name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Fatal crashes in Maryland, year to date",
       subtitle = "Running total of fatal crashes",
       x = NULL, y = "fatal crashes") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

```{r}
#Part 11 crashes by severity, 2024-2026: year to date AND full calendar year (clean Part 11)
# >>> severity_full_year is ARTICLE FACT CHECK 2 and is exported in OTHER EXPORTS
# one row per severity, one column per year, plus each severity's share of that year's crashes

severity_levels <- c("Fatal Crashes", "Injury Crashes", "Property Damage Crashes")

# ---- table 1: year to date, Jan 1 - YTD cutoff (Part 3) ----
severity_ytd <- report_2024 |>
  filter(NonTrafficFatal == "N") |>                      # on-road only, same as the other YTD tables
  mutate(crash_date = mdy(Crashdate),
         year = year(crash_date)) |>
  filter(crash_date <= make_date(year, ytd_month, ytd_day)) |>
  count(`Crash Severity Description`, year) |>           # crashes per severity per year
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = n) |>     # years become columns
  mutate(`Crash Severity Description` = factor(`Crash Severity Description`, levels = severity_levels)) |>
  arrange(`Crash Severity Description`) |>               # severity order instead of alphabetical
  # share of that year's crashes; sum() adds up the column, so this is row / year total
  mutate(pct_2024 = 100 * `2024` / sum(`2024`),
         pct_2025 = 100 * `2025` / sum(`2025`),
         pct_2026 = 100 * `2026` / sum(`2026`)) |>
  adorn_totals("row", name = "All crashes") |>           # janitor: adds a total row
  mutate(across(starts_with("pct_"), \(x) round(x, 2)))  # round LAST so the total row is exactly 100

# ---- table 2: full calendar year; 2026 is marked * because it's year to date ----
severity_full_year <- report_2024 |>
  filter(NonTrafficFatal == "N") |>
  mutate(crash_date = mdy(Crashdate),
         year = year(crash_date),
         year = if_else(year == 2026, "2026*", as.character(year))) |>   # label 2026 with the asterisk
  count(`Crash Severity Description`, year) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = n) |>
  mutate(`Crash Severity Description` = factor(`Crash Severity Description`, levels = severity_levels)) |>
  arrange(`Crash Severity Description`) |>
  mutate(pct_2024    = 100 * `2024`  / sum(`2024`),
         pct_2025    = 100 * `2025`  / sum(`2025`),
         `pct_2026*` = 100 * `2026*` / sum(`2026*`)) |>
  adorn_totals("row", name = "All crashes") |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("pct_"), \(x) round(x, 2)))

severity_ytd
severity_full_year     # printed again in ARTICLE FACT CHECK 2
```

```{r}
# Part 12 Graph fatalities as opposed to fatal accidents (clean Part 12)
# >>> fatalities_daily becomes FLOURISH GRAPHIC 1 (exported in 1A / 1B)
#running total of PEOPLE KILLED, whole state, full year 2024-2026
# same shape as the fatal crash version above, but one row per person, not per crash

fatalities_daily <- bind_rows(
  # people in vehicles who died
  occupants_2024 |>
    filter(`InjuryStatus Occ` == "01") |>      # 01 = Fatal Injury
    select(Reportnumber),
  # pedestrians, cyclists etc. who died -- they're NOT in the occupants table
  nonmotorists_2024 |>
    filter(`InjuryStatus NM` == "01") |>
    select(Reportnumber)
) |>
  # person tables have no date, so borrow it from the crash report.
  # NonTrafficFatal filter keeps the definition identical to the crash chart.
  inner_join(report_2024 |>
               filter(NonTrafficFatal == "N") |>
               select(Reportnumber, Crashdate),
             by = "Reportnumber") |>
  mutate(crash_date = mdy(Crashdate),
         year = year(crash_date),
         date = format(crash_date, "%m-%d")) |>
  # from here down, identical to fatal_crashes_daily
  count(date, year) |>
  complete(date = format(seq(ymd("2024-01-01"), ymd("2024-12-31"), by = "day"), "%m-%d"),
           year,
           fill = list(n = 0)) |>
  arrange(date) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  mutate(total = cumsum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(-n) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = total) |>
  mutate(`2026` = if_else(date > format(last_date, "%m-%d"), NA, `2026`))

fatalities_daily
```

```{r}
#Part 14 YTD summary, 2025 vs 2026: fatalities, fatal crashes, total crashes (clean Part 14)
# uses the YTD cutoff from Part 3. Printed in ARTICLE FACT CHECK 1.

# on-road crashes, Jan 1 - YTD cutoff, 2025 and 2026 only, with a year column
crashes_ytd_25_26 <- report_2024 |>
  filter(NonTrafficFatal == "N") |>
  mutate(crash_date = mdy(Crashdate),
         year = year(crash_date)) |>
  filter(year %in% c(2025, 2026),
         crash_date <= make_date(year, ytd_month, ytd_day))

# people killed in those crashes (occupants + non-motorists with Fatal Injury)
deaths_ytd_25_26 <- bind_rows(
  occupants_2024    |> filter(`InjuryStatus Occ` == "01") |> select(Reportnumber),
  nonmotorists_2024 |> filter(`InjuryStatus NM`  == "01") |> select(Reportnumber)
) |>
  inner_join(select(crashes_ytd_25_26, Reportnumber, year), by = "Reportnumber")

# one row per year. sum(condition) counts the rows where the condition is TRUE
ytd_counts <- tibble(
  year          = c("2025", "2026"),
  fatalities    = c(sum(deaths_ytd_25_26$year == 2025),
                    sum(deaths_ytd_25_26$year == 2026)),
  fatal_crashes = c(sum(crashes_ytd_25_26$year == 2025 & crashes_ytd_25_26$`Crash Severity Description` == "Fatal Crashes"),
                    sum(crashes_ytd_25_26$year == 2026 & crashes_ytd_25_26$`Crash Severity Description` == "Fatal Crashes")),
  total_crashes = c(sum(crashes_ytd_25_26$year == 2025),
                    sum(crashes_ytd_25_26$year == 2026))
)

# add a third row: percent change 2025 -> 2026 for each column
# x[1] is the 2025 value, x[2] is the 2026 value
ytd_summary <- bind_rows(
  ytd_counts,
  ytd_counts |>
    summarise(year = "pct_change",
              across(c(fatalities, fatal_crashes, total_crashes),
                     \(x) round(100 * (x[2] - x[1]) / x[1], 1)))
)
```

```{r}
#Part 15 identify causes (clean Part 16)

# ============================================================================
# ROLL-UP: MHSO emphasis-area flags onto report_2024
# Definitions: https://zerodeathsmd.gov/resources/crashdata/crashdashboard/dashboard-data-definitions/
#
# Each flag is built separately because each lives in a DIFFERENT table:
#   speed + aggressive -> contributing_circumstances_2024
#   distracted + unrestrained -> occupants_2024
#   impairment -> report_2024's own ImpairedCrash column (the state's flag)
#
# Every block follows the same three steps:
#   1. filter that table down to the rows that meet the definition
#   2. distinct(Reportnumber) -> collapse to ONE row per crash
#      (a crash with 3 speeding drivers should flag once, not three times)
#   3. mutate(flag = TRUE) -> a column to carry over in the join
# ============================================================================


# ---- AGGRESSIVE DRIVING -----------------------------------------------------
# MHSO: at least one driver showing >= TWO of these behaviors.
# Their published list is ACRS 1.0 wording; these are the ACRS 2.0 equivalents
# actually present in the data. "Exceeded speed limit" was eliminated in 2024.
aggressive_values <- c(
  "Failed to Yield Right-of-Way",                            # failed to yield ROW
  "Ran Stop Sign",                                           # was "failed to obey stop sign"
  "Ran Red Light",                                           # was "failed to obey traffic signal"
  "Disregarded Other Traffic Sign",                          # other traffic control
  "Wrong Side",                                              # was "failed to keep right of center"
  "Failed To Stop For School Bus",
  "Too Fast For Conditions",
  "Followed Too Closely",
  "Failed to Keep in Proper Lane",                           # closest to "improper lane change"
  "Improper Passing",
  "Disregard Officer Directions",
  "Disregarded Other Road Markings",
  "Other Improper Action",
  "Operated Motor Vehicle in Reckless or Aggressive Manner"  # "erratic/reckless"
)

flag_aggressive <- contributing_circumstances_2024 |>
  filter(`Contribs Type` == "Driver",                    # driver actions only, not road/weather/vehicle
         `Contribs Description` %in% aggressive_values) |>
  # distinct() first so the same behavior logged twice for one driver isn't double-counted
  distinct(Reportnumber, `Person ID Contribs`, `Contribs Description`) |>
  count(Reportnumber, `Person ID Contribs`) |>           # how many DIFFERENT behaviors per driver
  filter(n >= 2) |>                                      # the ">= two" test, per driver
  distinct(Reportnumber) |>
  mutate(aggressive_driving = TRUE)


# ---- SPEED RELATED ----------------------------------------------------------
# MHSO 2024 update: "Exceeded the speed limit" is no longer an attribute, so from
# 2024 onward this counts ONLY "too fast for conditions". One value, no >=2 rule.
flag_speed <- contributing_circumstances_2024 |>
  filter(`Contribs Type` == "Driver",
         `Contribs Description` == "Too Fast For Conditions") |>
  distinct(Reportnumber) |>
  mutate(speed_related = TRUE)


# ---- DISTRACTED DRIVING -----------------------------------------------------
# ACRS 2.0 replaced the old fields with "Distracted By Action". MHSO counts a
# driver as distracted on any affirmative value there.
# NOTE: this field is only ever populated for drivers, never passengers, so no
# extra driver filter is needed. "Not Distracted" and "Unknown" are excluded.
flag_distracted <- occupants_2024 |>
  filter(`TypeOfOccupant Description` == "Driver",
         `DistractedByAction Occ Description` %in% c(
    "Texting",
    "Talking/listening",
    "Manually Operating (dialing, playing game, etc.)",
    "Other Action (looking away from task, etc.)"
  )) |>
  distinct(Reportnumber) |>
  mutate(distracted_driving = TRUE)


# ---- IMPAIRMENT -------------------------------------------------------------
# Uses the state's own flag, ImpairedCrash (Yes/No), already on every crash report.
# It includes Person Condition ("Under the Influence of Alcohol, Drugs, and/or
# Medication"), which isn't in the public export, so we can't rebuild it ourselves.
flag_impaired <- report_2024 |>
  filter(ImpairedCrash == "Yes") |>
  distinct(Reportnumber) |>
  mutate(impairment = TRUE)


# ---- UNRESTRAINED OCCUPANTS -------------------------------------------------
# MHSO: "Persons (vehicle occupants only), who are FATALLY INJURED ... where the
# Safety Equipment Used field was indicated to be 'None.' Drivers of
# motorcycles, ATVs, or mopeds are not included."
#
# The exclusion needs vehicle body type, which lives in vehicles_2024.
# occupants_2024$`VehicleID Occ` links to vehicles_2024$VehicleID.

# vehicles where a restraint doesn't apply, so "None" isn't a finding
no_restraint_vehicles <- c(
  "Motorcycle - 2 Wheeled",
  "Motorcycle - 3 Wheeled",
  "Moped Or motorized bicycle",
  "All-Terrain Vehicle/All-Terrain Cycle (ATV/ATC)"
)

flag_unrestrained <- occupants_2024 |>
  filter(`Restraint Occ Description` == "None",
         `InjuryStatus Occ` == "01") |>                    # 01 = Fatal Injury
  # pull in body type; select() first so we don't drag 69 vehicle columns along
  left_join(select(vehicles_2024, VehicleID, `BodyType Veh Description`),
            by = c("VehicleID Occ" = "VehicleID")) |>
  # MHSO excludes DRIVERS of these vehicles -- passengers on them still count
  filter(!(`TypeOfOccupant Description` == "Driver" &
           `BodyType Veh Description` %in% no_restraint_vehicles)) |>
  distinct(Reportnumber) |>
  mutate(unrestrained = TRUE)


# ---- JOIN ALL FIVE ONTO report_2024 -----------------------------------------
# left_join keeps every crash and attaches TRUE where the flag table has a match.
# Crashes with no match get NA, so replace_na() turns those into FALSE --
# otherwise sum() and filter() on these columns behave unpredictably.
report_2024_flagged <- report_2024 |>
  left_join(flag_speed,        by = "Reportnumber") |>
  left_join(flag_aggressive,   by = "Reportnumber") |>
  left_join(flag_distracted,   by = "Reportnumber") |>
  left_join(flag_impaired,     by = "Reportnumber") |>
  left_join(flag_unrestrained, by = "Reportnumber") |>
  mutate(across(c(speed_related, aggressive_driving, distracted_driving,
                  impairment, unrestrained), ~ replace_na(.x, FALSE))) |>
  # a sixth flag: TRUE when none of the five above are set.
  # MUST come after the replace_na() above -- !NA is NA, so if the FALSEs
  # weren't filled in first this column would be full of NAs.
  mutate(no_category = !speed_related & !aggressive_driving &
                       !distracted_driving & !impairment & !unrestrained)


# sanity check: should match the number of rows in report_2024. If it grew, a flag
# table had duplicate Reportnumbers and the distinct() step failed somewhere.
nrow(report_2024_flagged)
```

```{r}
#Part 16 causes by county and causes by county year to date (clean Part 17)
# ---- causes_by_county: FULL YEAR -------------------------------------------
# straight from report_2024_flagged -- no fatal_ytd in between
causes_by_county <- report_2024_flagged |>
  # fatal, on-roadway crashes only
  filter(NonTrafficFatal == "N",
         `Crash Severity Description` == "Fatal Crashes") |>
  # turn the text date into a real date, and pull out the year
  mutate(crash_date = mdy(Crashdate),
         year = year(crash_date)) |>
  # one bucket per county-year, then collapse each bucket to one row
  group_by(county = `Crash County Description`, year) |>
  summarise(
    fatal_crashes  = n(),
    n_speed        = sum(speed_related),
    n_aggressive   = sum(aggressive_driving),
    n_distracted   = sum(distracted_driving),
    n_impairment   = sum(impairment),
    n_unrestrained = sum(unrestrained),
    n_no_category  = sum(no_category),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    pct_speed        = round(100 * n_speed        / fatal_crashes, 1),
    pct_aggressive   = round(100 * n_aggressive   / fatal_crashes, 1),
    pct_distracted   = round(100 * n_distracted   / fatal_crashes, 1),
    pct_impairment   = round(100 * n_impairment   / fatal_crashes, 1),
    pct_unrestrained = round(100 * n_unrestrained / fatal_crashes, 1),
    pct_no_category  = round(100 * n_no_category  / fatal_crashes, 1)
  ) |>
  # 2026 minus 2024, on the 2026 row only. group_by(county) lets each row
  # see the other years of its own county. sum() of the 2024 value instead
  # of the value itself so a county with no 2024 row counts as 0, not an error.
  group_by(county) |>
  mutate(change_26_vs_24 = if_else(year == 2026,
                                   fatal_crashes - sum(fatal_crashes[year == 2024]),
                                   NA)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(county, year)


# ---- causes_by_county_ytd: JAN 1 - YTD CUTOFF -----------------------------
# identical to the one above EXCEPT the one line marked below
causes_by_county_ytd <- report_2024_flagged |>
  filter(NonTrafficFatal == "N",
         `Crash Severity Description` == "Fatal Crashes") |>
  mutate(crash_date = mdy(Crashdate),
         year = year(crash_date)) |>
  filter(crash_date <= make_date(year, ytd_month, ytd_day)) |>      # <-- THE ONLY DIFFERENCE
  group_by(county = `Crash County Description`, year) |>
  summarise(
    fatal_crashes  = n(),
    n_speed        = sum(speed_related),
    n_aggressive   = sum(aggressive_driving),
    n_distracted   = sum(distracted_driving),
    n_impairment   = sum(impairment),
    n_unrestrained = sum(unrestrained),
    n_no_category  = sum(no_category),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    pct_speed        = round(100 * n_speed        / fatal_crashes, 1),
    pct_aggressive   = round(100 * n_aggressive   / fatal_crashes, 1),
    pct_distracted   = round(100 * n_distracted   / fatal_crashes, 1),
    pct_impairment   = round(100 * n_impairment   / fatal_crashes, 1),
    pct_unrestrained = round(100 * n_unrestrained / fatal_crashes, 1),
    pct_no_category  = round(100 * n_no_category  / fatal_crashes, 1)
  ) |>
  group_by(county) |>
  mutate(change_26_vs_24 = if_else(year == 2026,
                                   fatal_crashes - sum(fatal_crashes[year == 2024]),
                                   NA)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(county, year)

causes_by_county
causes_by_county_ytd
```

```{r}
#Part 17 statewide fatal crashes by cause, year to date (Jan 1 - YTD cutoff) (clean Part 18)
# >>> statewide_causes_ytd_wide becomes FLOURISH GRAPHIC 5 (exported in 5A / 5B)
# builds two versions of the same numbers from causes_by_county_ytd:
#   statewide_causes_ytd_wide -> years as rows, causes as columns
#   statewide_causes_ytd      -> causes as rows, years as columns

cause_order <- c("All fatal crashes", "Impairment", "Aggressive driving",
                 "Unrestrained occupants", "Speed related",
                 "Distracted driving", "None of the five")

# years as rows: add up the 24 counties into one statewide row per year,
# then give the columns readable names
statewide_causes_ytd_wide <- causes_by_county_ytd |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(across(c(fatal_crashes, starts_with("n_")), sum)) |>
  rename(`All fatal crashes`      = fatal_crashes,
         Impairment               = n_impairment,
         `Aggressive driving`     = n_aggressive,
         `Unrestrained occupants` = n_unrestrained,
         `Speed related`          = n_speed,
         `Distracted driving`     = n_distracted,
         `None of the five`       = n_no_category) |>
  select(year, all_of(cause_order))                       # put the columns in cause_order

# causes as rows: flip the table above (long, then wide the other way)
statewide_causes_ytd <- statewide_causes_ytd_wide |>
  pivot_longer(-year, names_to = "cause", values_to = "crashes") |>
  mutate(cause = factor(cause, levels = cause_order)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = crashes) |>
  arrange(cause)

statewide_causes_ytd_wide
statewide_causes_ytd
```

```{r}
#Part 18 Causes by county, top cause (clean Part 19)

# leading 2024 cause per county
#
# Filters:
#   - from causes_by_county_ytd: Jan 1 - YTD cutoff, traffic fatal crashes only
#   - counties with MORE than 20 fatal crashes in 2024
#   - leading cause = the flag with the most 2024 fatal crashes (no_category excluded)

# causes_by_county names its columns n_speed etc.; this matches them to the flag names
cause_names <- c(n_speed        = "speed_related",
                 n_aggressive   = "aggressive_driving",
                 n_distracted   = "distracted_driving",
                 n_impairment   = "impairment",
                 n_unrestrained = "unrestrained")

top_causes <- causes_by_county_ytd |>
  filter(year == 2024, fatal_crashes>20) |>
  select(county, all_of(names(cause_names))) |>
  pivot_longer(-county, names_to = "cause", values_to = "n") |>
  mutate(cause = unname(cause_names[cause])) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 1, by = county, with_ties = FALSE)

top_causes     # printed again in ARTICLE FACT CHECK 4
```

```{r}
# Part 19: each county's leading cause, fatal crashes per year (Jan 1 - YTD cutoff) (clean Part 20)
# >>> top_cause_yearly_wide becomes FLOURISH GRAPHIC 4 (exported in 4A / 4B)

top_cause_yearly <- causes_by_county_ytd |>
  select(county, year, all_of(names(cause_names))) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(county, year), names_to = "cause", values_to = "n") |>
  mutate(cause = unname(cause_names[cause])) |>
  inner_join(select(top_causes, county, cause), by = c("county", "cause")) |>
  mutate(series = paste0(county, " - ", cause))

# wide table for Flourish: year in column 1, one column per county
top_cause_yearly_wide <- top_cause_yearly |>
  select(year, series, n) |>
```

```{r}
# Part 21 more detail on impairment progress (clean Part 22)
# >>> top_cause_daily_wide is not a Flourish graphic; it is exported in OTHER EXPORTS
#
# Full year for 2024 and 2025; 2026 stops at last_date (needs last_date from Part 7 run first)

top_cause_daily <- report_2024_flagged |>
  filter(NonTrafficFatal == "N",
         `Crash Severity Description` == "Fatal Crashes") |>
  mutate(crash_date = mdy(Crashdate),
         year = year(crash_date),
         date = format(crash_date, "%m-%d")) |>
  rename(county = `Crash County Description`) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(unname(cause_names)), names_to = "cause", values_to = "flag") |>
  filter(flag) |>
  inner_join(select(top_causes, county, cause), by = c("county", "cause")) |>
  count(county, cause, year, date) |>
  # every calendar day for every county/year, 0 on days with no crashes
  complete(nesting(county, cause), year,
           date = format(seq(ymd("2024-01-01"), ymd("2024-12-31"), by = "day"), "%m-%d"),
           fill = list(n = 0)) |>
  arrange(county, year, date) |>
  group_by(county, cause, year) |>
  mutate(total = cumsum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(total = if_else(year == 2026 & date > format(last_date, "%m-%d"), NA, total),
         series = paste0(county, " - ", cause))

# wide table: date in column 1, one column per county + year
top_cause_daily_wide <- top_cause_daily |>
  mutate(column = paste0(series, " - ", year)) |>
  select(date, column, total) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = total)

top_cause_daily_wide

top_cause_daily |>

  ggplot(aes(x = plot_date, y = total, color = factor(year))) +

                     name = NULL) +

       subtitle = paste0("Counties with 20+ fatal crashes in 2024 (Jan 1 - ", ytd_label, ")"),
       x = NULL, y = "fatal crashes") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

```{r}
#    B01003_001 = total population. acs1 = the single-year survey, which
#    matches a single year of deaths better than the default 5-year average.

                    year = 2023, survey = "acs1") |>
  select(state_fips = GEOID, pop_2023 = estimate)
```

```{r}
#Part 25 FARS deaths by state (clean Part 25, steps 1-7; steps 8-10 are in FLOURISH GRAPHIC 6B)
# >>> fars_national becomes FLOURISH GRAPHIC 6 (exported in 6A / 6B)
# 1. import
fars_national <- read_csv('FARS/FARS national.csv')

# 3. state abbreviation + FIPS code, placed before the State column.
#    fips_codes is a lookup table that ships with tidycensus; distinct()
#    because it has one row per COUNTY and we only need one per state.
fars_national <- fars_national |>
  left_join(distinct(fips_codes, state_name, state, state_code),
            by = c("State" = "state_name")) |>
  # the national "USA" row has no match in the lookup, so fill it by hand
  mutate(state      = if_else(State == "USA", "US", state),
         state_code = if_else(State == "USA", "00", state_code)) |>
  relocate(state_abbr = state, state_fips = state_code, .before = State)

fars_national <- fars_national |>
  left_join(pop_2023, by = "state_fips") |>
  left_join(pop_2024, by = "state_fips") |>
  # USA row: add up the 50 states + DC
  mutate(pop_2023 = if_else(State == "USA", sum(pop_2023[State != "USA"]), pop_2023),
         pop_2024 = if_else(State == "USA", sum(pop_2024[State != "USA"]), pop_2024)) |>

# 5. deaths per 100,000 residents
  mutate(deaths_per_100k_2023 = `2023` / pop_2023 * 100000,
         deaths_per_100k_2024 = `2024` / pop_2024 * 100000,
# 6. percent change in that rate, 2023 to 2024
         pct_change_per_100k  = 100 * (deaths_per_100k_2024 - deaths_per_100k_2023) /
                                deaths_per_100k_2023,
# 7. rank of the 2024 rate, highest = 1. The USA row is set to NA before
#    ranking, so it is excluded and gets NA instead of a rank.
         rank_deaths_per_100k_2024 = min_rank(desc(
           if_else(State == "USA", NA_real_, deaths_per_100k_2024)))) |>
  # round LAST, so the percent change and rank are calculated from unrounded rates
  mutate(across(c(deaths_per_100k_2023, deaths_per_100k_2024), ~ round(.x, 2)),
         pct_change_per_100k = round(pct_change_per_100k, 1)) |>
  relocate(rank_deaths_per_100k_2024, .after = deaths_per_100k_2024)

fars_national
```

```{r}
#FLOURISH GRAPHIC 4B for Flourish
# Upload this file to Flourish, not 4A.
# Shortens the county column names for Flourish ("Anne Arundel - impairment" -> "Anne Arundel")
# and marks Baltimore City with an asterisk for its popup note.
# Then adds one "... change" column per county: the % change vs. 2024, as a short
# colored line of HTML for the popup (blank in 2024). In Flourish, the county
# columns go under Values and the "... change" columns under Info for popups.
#
# add_change_html() is defined here and reused in 5B.
# Red + up arrow = more than 2024, teal + down arrow = fewer, same colors as the FARS popup.
add_change_html <- function(df) {
  df |>
    mutate(across(-year, \(x) {
      p     <- round((x - x[year == 2024]) / x[year == 2024] * 100, 1)
      color <- case_when(p > 0 ~ "#c71e1d", p < 0 ~ "#0f7b74", TRUE ~ "#666666")
      arrow <- case_when(p > 0 ~ "▲ ", p < 0 ~ "▼ ", TRUE ~ "")
      if_else(year == 2024, "",
              paste0("<span style='font-weight:700;color:", color, ";'>", arrow, abs(p), "%</span>",
                     " vs. this time in 2024"))
    }, .names = "{.col} change"))
}

top_cause_yearly_wide |>
  rename_with(\(name) str_remove(name, " - impairment")) |>   # drop " - impairment" from the 6 county names
  rename(`Baltimore City*` = `Baltimore City`) |>              # asterisk for the popup note
  add_change_html() |>
  export("output/flourish_4_top_cause_yearly_wide.csv")
```

```{r}
#FLOURISH GRAPHIC 5A raw
# Graphic 5: Maryland fatal crashes by MHSO cause, statewide, Jan 1 - YTD cutoff, 2024-2026
# Built in Part 17. One row per year, one column per cause, plus "All fatal crashes".
# A crash can count under more than one cause, so the causes don't add up to the total.
export(statewide_causes_ytd_wide, "output/statewide_causes_ytd_wide.csv")
```

```{r}
#FLOURISH GRAPHIC 5B for Flourish
# Upload this file to Flourish, not 5A.
# Adds one "... change" column per cause: the % change vs. 2024, as a short
# colored line of HTML for the popup (blank in 2024). In Flourish, the cause
# columns go under Values and the "... change" columns under Info for popups.
# Needs add_change_html() from 4B, so run 4B first.
export(add_change_html(statewide_causes_ytd_wide), "output/flourish_5_statewide_causes_ytd_wide.csv")
```

```{r}
#FLOURISH GRAPHIC 6A raw
# Graphic 6: traffic deaths per 100,000 residents by state, 2024, and the change since 2023
# Built in Part 25 from FARS deaths + Census populations. One row per state + DC,
# plus a USA row. Rank 1 = highest death rate; the USA row isn't ranked.
export(fars_national, "output/fars_national.csv")
```

```{r}
#FLOURISH GRAPHIC 6B for Flourish (clean Part 25, steps 8-10)
# Upload this file to Flourish, not 6A.
# Adds the popup pieces the map's tooltip uses (arrow + % text, wording, color,
# rank badge colors), then renames two columns to the display names shown in
# Flourish's buttons and popup.
fars_national_flourish <- fars_national |>
# 8. tooltip pieces for the change stat. A tooltip can't choose a color or
#    an arrow by itself, so build them here: red + up arrow if the rate rose,
#    teal + down arrow if it fell. Built from the rounded value so they match
#    the number shown on the map.
  mutate(rose = pct_change_per_100k > 0,
         change_pct_text = paste0(if_else(rose, "▲ ", "▼ "),
                                  sprintf("%.1f", abs(pct_change_per_100k)), "%"),
         change_words    = if_else(rose, "more deaths per resident",
                                         "fewer deaths per resident"),
         change_color    = if_else(rose, "#c71e1d", "#0f7b74")) |>
  select(-rose) |>
# 9. rank band (5 groups of ~10 states) and the badge colors for that band.
#    Badge colors match the popup's spectrum bar (red = highest death rates),
#    so the badge and the marker under it are always the same color.
#    Text color is set per band so the badge stays readable on every fill.
  mutate(rank_band  = case_when(rank_deaths_per_100k_2024 <= 10 ~ 1,
                                rank_deaths_per_100k_2024 <= 20 ~ 2,
                                rank_deaths_per_100k_2024 <= 31 ~ 3,
                                rank_deaths_per_100k_2024 <= 41 ~ 4,
                                rank_deaths_per_100k_2024 <= 51 ~ 5),
         badge_bg   = c("#c71e1d", "#e8661a", "#faa916", "#c3d36a", "#8fd694")[rank_band],
         badge_text = c("#ffffff", "#1a1a1a", "#1a1a1a", "#1a1a1a", "#1a1a1a")[rank_band]) |>
# 10. rename to the display names used in Flourish (control buttons + tooltip).
#     Done LAST so every calculation above can use the plain names.
  rename(`Deaths per 100k residents (2024)` = deaths_per_100k_2024,
         `% Change (2023-2024)`             = pct_change_per_100k)

export(fars_national_flourish, "output/flourish_6_fars_national.csv")
```
